newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Access says Australian budget neutral for markets.
newsitem.headline: Access says Australian budget neutral for markets.

text.p: Private forecaster Access Economics said on Wednesday that the Australian government's 1997/98 budget was "relaxed and complacent" and would probably be neutral for financial markets.

Access director David Chessell told a budget briefing that the underlying strategy of the budget was to offend no-one, rely on cyclical forces, and wait for the next financial year to dish out "pre-election goodies".

"If (Treasurer Peter) Costello had just said 'the budget is cancelled' yesterday, the numbers would have been very similar to what we have now," Chessell said, referring to the A$352 million net savings effect of new measures in the document.
"It is the (economic) cycle the government is pinning its hopes on for pushing the budget into surplus in the years ahead."
Chessell said he believed the budget's economic forecasts, estimates of tax collection and proceeds of assets sales were slightly on the pessimistic side.
"I think there is a reasonable chance....of some kind of rabbit coming out of the hat and paying for a pre-election tax cut in the May 1998 budget," he said.

"I suspect overall the budget is probably neutral for the market and that our interest rates are going to be more determined by what happens (at the United States Reserve Bank meeting) on May 20," he said, adding that Access expected long rates to be a little higher 12-18 months out.
